entries.sign: The system of tens is universally used by our Indians in enumeration. In counting from one to ten, the usual way is to hold the closed right hand in front, the back towards and about height of shoulder, edges of hand pointing up; for one, the little finger is extended; two, the third; three, second; four, index; five, thumb; keeping fingers extended, separated, and pointing upwards; six, bring the closed left hand at same height, equally advanced, and near right, and extend the thumb; seven, extend left index; eight, second finger; nine, third finger; ten, little finger. For twenty, open and close both hands twice. Many tribes indicate a number of tens by first making the sign for ten, then hold extended left hand horizontally in front of body, and draw the tip of extended right index from base over the back of each finger to its tip, each motion of this kind representing ten and going as far as fifty; then holding the right hand in similar manner, mark the backs of its thumb and fingers with tip of left index to indicate from sixty to one hundred. For counting hundreds hold up both 5 hands with both thumbs touching, hands held near right shoulder; then swing in a circle across to left and downwards. A number of hundreds are counted on backs of hands same as in counting tens, first indicating that you are now dealing with hundreds.

entries.sign: Two signs have been used in this connection, for that in most general use sign BIRD and INDIAN. A less used sign as follows:—first make the sign for INDIAN, then hold fist above forehead, palm out, to indicate their manner of dressing the hair, i. e., pompadour.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: tears). With both 1 hands at eyes indicate that tears are flowing by tracing their course down the face.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for WOLF.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With flat left hand, back upwards, held in front of left breast, use right flat hand as though to cut slice off palm of left, and repeat.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (See SIOUX.)
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for RIVER, and for HOLD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: hopping action). Place both 5 hands in front of breast, point- ing up, palms 6 inches apart; move up and down 3 inches, for 2 or 3 times.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With respect to a person, make the signs HEART and BAD. If of a place, specify in what way it is dangerous.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for NIGHT and SAME; or hold extended hands in front of and close to eyes.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for FEMALE, then with right compressed hand held upright indicate the height of girl.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold level flat hands, backs up, in front of face, and 4 inches apart; sweep hands up and out in a curve, ending opposite shoulders with palms up. For TODAY, first make sign NOW.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Place both extended hands, backs out, in same horizontal plane, right hand above with little finger touching left index; then raise the right hand a few inches.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for DIE and SLEEP.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Press palm of flat right hand against right ear; then make small circular motion with hand close to ear, and sign NO.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: he gives the lie). Make sign for GIVE and for LIE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: To show depth of river or water, make sign for RIVER or WATER; then point downwards. If depth is slight, place hand on person to show how far the water rises on person or horse.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Indicate deer horns with both spread 5 hands held above sides of head.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for ABUSE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Place thumb between index and second finger of right hand; push it sharply towards the person.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for GO.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for EXTERMINATE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: going under). Hold the left flat hand, back out, well in front of body, fingers horizontal; bring right 1 hand on same plane and pointing to left hand, move right hand downwards and outwards.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Execute with both hands a pawing motion, moving hands from right front down- wards, to left and rear on curve; repeating motion.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: See EAT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Point to ground with right index finger, then reach down and rub thumb and tips of fingers together.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for HEART and TIRED. The head is sometimes turned to one side, and the idea conveyed by facial expression.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for HORSE; then raise right 2 hand and lower it, pointing fingers at ground.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Right hand, back to right, in front of right breast, a little lower than shoulder, hand partly closed and close to body; push the hand to front, raising it slightly. Very distant would be shown by extending arm to full length.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: handing out). Bring right flat hand, back of same to right, well in front and a little to right of body; move hand slightly upwards to front, and then a little downwards; then take first position and make similar motion to left, as though giving to several persons.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold left flat hand, back outwards, well in front of body, fingers pointing to right; hold right flat hand, back out, behind and little above left hand, fingers pointing downward; then move right hand down and out under left hand.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for HIS, WOMAN, and ABANDONED.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WORK.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for WORK and NO.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for WHITE MAN, CHIEF and MEDICINE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: wolf drawing teepee poles). Draw right 2 hand across in front of body, from left to right.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for MONEY, and raise right index finger to indicate one.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for END.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for TEEPEE or for HOUSE; hold left flat hand well in front of breast, back outwards and pointing to right; then place flat right hand on palm, and turn same over to right, as though little finger was a hinge.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for PERHAPS.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Point downwards with right index finger.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for SLEEP, and SEE, and GOOD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Pass the spread thumb and index finger over that part of body represented as covered.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: drinking from the curved right hand). With fingers tight together partly compress the right hand as though to form a cup; carry to mouth from above downwards, as though drinking water.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for LONGTIME, RAIN, and NO.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WATER; then sign whether LAKE or RIVER, and make sign for DIE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Place hands in first motion for KETTLE; then with left hand still in posi- tion, use partly closed right hand as drum-stick, and strike down several times.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for WHISKEY and sign for DRINK, repeating four or five times, and signs for MUCH and CRAZY.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: To indicate that stream or spring is dry, make sign for STREAM (LITTLE RIVER), for WATER, and for ALL GONE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for BIRD and WATER, and gesture with right flat hand for flat hill.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold left flat hand in front of body, back down; then with lower edge of flat right hand saw back and forth 3 or 4 times; then make sign for BAD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Palm of right hand over mouth; then make the signs TALK and NO.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: wings, and black tips of tail feathers). Make sign for BIRD; then hold horizontally the extended left flat hand, back up, in front of left breast, fingers pointing to front and right; then lay the lower edge of vertical extended right hand, back to right and outwards, fingers pointing to left and front, on back of left, on knuckles; move the right hand outwards and to right; then make sign for BLACK, representing the black end of the tail feathers. Occasionally the sign for TAÍL is made.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: If early in the morning make signs for DAYBREAK, and LITTLE; if early in the evening, make signs for SUNSET, and LITTLE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: long, narrow pendant). Point extended index fingers down- ward, other fingers and thumbs closed, alongside of ears, backs of hands towards head; shake hands a trifle, giving a trembling motion to index fingers.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Point with right index to the ground, then reach down and rub thumb and tips of fingers together.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With nearly compressed right hand, pass tips of fingers in curve downward past mouth two or three times by wrist action. Add location of sun in the sky to indicate breakfast, dinner or supper. (Modern).
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: filled to the throat). Make the sign for EAT; then spread index and thumb of right hand close to breast; move the hand upwards to height of chin.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for PUSH.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: horns). With fingers extended and pointing upwards, place hands above head; move them to front and rear two or three times.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: The Indian method of eloping is to STEAL the woman; so the proper signs are accordingly made, i.e., STEAL and WOMAN.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: cut off). Hold left flat hand out in front of left breast, thumb up- ward; then with right flat hand strike down past finger tips of left hand.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs FRIEND and NO. Have seen Indians make the signs SHAKE HANDS and NO, though first sign is more general.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for WORK and SOLDIER.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: to enter a TEEPEE, or stooping position in entering a lodge). Make sign for HOUSE; then hold compressed left hand well in front of body; bring partly compressed right hand downwards and outwards, under left.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: even race). Hold 1 hands in front of breast, indexes two inches apart; move them both to front, keeping tips opposite, indicating an even race.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With hands closed, cross the wrists; then separate hands quickly by swing ing them to right and left and slightly upwards; then make the sign for GO.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for FOREVER.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With extended right hand, make the sign of SUN sinking in the west; then signs NIGHT, and LITTLE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold up 1 hands; then in semi-circle strike them past each other.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold extended right hand, back down, in front of, close to, and little lower than mouth, fingers pointing to left; by wrist action move hand outwards a few inches. To be spoken to or explained to, reverse the action, moving hand to- wards face.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: wiped out). Hold left flat hand in front of body; then wipe flat right hand across same.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Bring right flat hand down across front of face.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for DIE and for RECOVER.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (Season). Make sign for AUTUMN.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (of water). Make sign for RIVER; then hold flat hand, back out, in front of body; bring right hand, fingers slightly apart, over top of left hand and down with wavy motion.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (to). Right flat hand in front of body, pointing to left, back up; swing hand in a curve, upwards and outwards, to right, then downwards while turning hand palm up.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: The highest compliment you can pay an Indian is to say that he is a CHIEF, BRAVE; therefore make these signs to express fame.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for DISTANT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for CORN and for WORK.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: pass by). Hold left flat hand in front of body, back to left; then hold right flat hand, back to right, six inches to rear of left. Make right hand go swiftly past left in a curve very slightly downwards and then upwards.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With compressed right hand gently tap right breast two or three times; then make the sign for MALE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WIFE or HUSBAND, then FATHER.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for AFRAID.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for WORK, for two or three kettles in a row, for BRING (from several directions); first part of sign for COUNCIL, and for EAT. (Repeat this latter two or three times).
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: For one feather worn as a decoration on the head, make sign for BIRD, for TAIL, and place extended index of right hand pointing up at back of head.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: combing the hair). Place both hands on either side of head, fingers hooked; then stroke downwards as though combing the hair. Use of but right hand also correct.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: compressed). Hold partly closed hands in front of body, palms towards each other, lower edges pointing to front, hands opposite, but heel of right hand height of index of left, and eight inches apart; move right hand to left, left to right until right is over left.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Bring loose fists, palms toward each other, in front of body, at height of shoulders, and three inches apart. Move right hand few inches towards body, while left goes outwards same distance; then reverse and repeat.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for END.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: blaze). Carry right arm well down in front of body, fingers par- tially closed; raise hand slightly and snap fingers upwards. Repeat.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: discharge of weapon). See SHOOT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for WATER, then hold flat right hand, back to right, at right of body near waist; then move the hand to front sinuously.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold left flat hand upwards, right flat hand crossing it at right angles; push edge of right across left, while left flattens with back up.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Bring right flat hand out in front right shoulder; place fingers of left hand on wrist of right, then oscillate or wave right hand several times.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Indicate the WATER, RIVER, LAKE, etc. Bring extended left hand in front of breast, back up; lay right hand on it; then move hands with wavy motion to right.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold right hand, back to right, in front of body, and rub tips of fingers with tip of thumb; then point to something white and make sign for BREAD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for GRASS at waistline. Then make circle of thumb and index of both hands; then turn outside of hands under, until little fingers touch and thumbs and indexes point up. Some add SMELL and GOOD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for WINGS, as in BIRD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for WATER; then cross hands, fingers open, in front of eyes.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With palms facing, left hand ahead, thrust both hands forward with zigzag motion.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: pressed to the heart). Cross wrists, a little in front and above the heart, right nearest body, hands closed, backs out; press right forearm against body and left wrist against right. This expresses regard, liking, fondness, affec- tion and love.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for EAT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for CRAZY. (For UNWISE, INDISCREET or FOOLISH, add sign for LITTLE.)
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for WALK and for SEE; fingers pointing to ground.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for RUN and for EQUAL. If one comes out ahead, move one finger to front.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold open right and left hands ten inches out in front of shoulders, back outward, thunb and fingers spread. Move slightly upward, slowly, to indicate growth, then extend right hand to right and front indicating trees extend great dis- tance, then add PLENTY.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Place the open right hand, palm towards right side of head, just clear of head; then move it forward and backward twice, past front and rear of head. In general use fifty years ago, according to Hadley.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: mental darkness). Almost make sign for NIGHT, by holding left hand steady in front and sweeping right hand around to left.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: white soldier's house). Make the sign for WHITE, for SOLDIER, and for HOUSE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: This is represented by I SAW IT, PICKED IT UP.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Show size of animal and large, long tail with white tip.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: smells good). Move the right 2 hand by wrist action upwards from chin, nose passing between tips of fingers; then sign GOOD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for COLD, for WATER, and for HARD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: ice closing over a stream). Make sign for COLD and for WATER or RIVER; then hold flat hands, backs up, opposite shoulders, fingers pointing to front; move hands toward each other until index fingers touch. Representing ice formed on surface of water.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: brothers growing up together). Hold right hand in front of neck, palm outwards, index and second fingers extending upwards; raise the hand until tips of fingers are high as head. Southern Indians make sign of shaking their own hands, which all Indians now understand.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for WATER; then compress right hand near right shoulder and make motion of frog jumping.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (Meaning—time in front.) Make the sign for TIME, then advance the right hand past and beyond the left hand.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for RIDE; then bring hands in front of center of body, hands held edgewise, left near the body, right in front of same; move the hands simultan- eously up and down several times in vertical curves, to imitate action of horse.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: mountain pass). With index and thumb spread, hold left hand out in front of breast, in form of gap; then pass right hand edgewise through the gap.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for HEART and BIG.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for POSSESSION.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WOMAN; then bring hand down on right side to indicate height; fingers compressed and pointing up.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold right flat hand, back to right, pointing to front and upwards, in front of body at height of shoulder; move hand out and down.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: About height of neck, bring right well out in front of body, back of hand downwards and slightly to left, lower edge nearest to body, hand flat and point- ing upwards; bring hand in towards body and lower slightly.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for CALL and GIVE. Clark says: “A young man, after making his maiden effort on the war path, if he has met with success, 'sheds' his boyish name, and is given frequently the name by which some of the old men of his tribe have always been known.”
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: sunshine in the heart). Make sign for HEART; then sign for DAY or OPENING UP, and SUNRISE. By carrying hands into position on curves as indicated gives grace and beauty to movements.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: the clouds are close). Make the sign for CLOUDS; then draw them down to near the head.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Pass the spread thumb and index of right over left hand, meaning any covering for the hands.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold flat right hand in front of body, back to right, pointing front and down- wards; move hand to front, and by wrist action, raise fingers to front and upwards.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for PUSH.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: horns, and whiskers under chin). Bring 1 hands alongside of head, pointing upwards, hands held just over ears; then place back of right wrist against under side of chin, hand compressed and pointing downward.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: the great mystery). Make signs for MEDICINE and GREAT, and point to zenith.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for MONEY; then point to something YELLOW in color.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for GO and LONG TIME.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: level with the heart). Hold the flat right hand, back up, in front of and close to left breast, pointing to left; move hand briskly well out to front and to right, keeping it in a horizontal plane.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for GOOD, DAY and SUNSET. (The true Indian version would be SUNSET, DAY and GOOD.)
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for GOOD, DAY and SUNRISE. (To be exact, the Indian would say SUNRISE, DAY, and GOOD.)
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make slow sign for BIRD; then indicate triangular shape taken by flocks of geese in their migrations.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for FATHER, and for OLD, by, rotating right hand by right ear to indicate that hearing was poor.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for MOTHER, and for OLD, by rotating right hand by right ear to indicate that hearing was poor.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold the hands, back downwards, arms extended downwards to full length, in front of body, fingers extended, separated and slightly curved, pointing upwards; then swing hands apart.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for DIE and BURY.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: white and black). Make the signs for WHITE, LITTLE, BLACK, LITTLE, or make sign for COLOR and point to something gray.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With palms toward each other bring extended hands out in front of breast; then separate the hands to right and left.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for MEDICINE and GREAT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for COLOR; then point to the grass if convenient, otherwise to something green.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for CRY, and for cutting off hair.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold right hand, back down, index extended, and pointing upwards, in front of body; hand held near the ground; raise hand by gentle jerks.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make as though shooting gun, then add sign for FIRE. For rifle add working of lever.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for RAIN, for COLD; then indicate size of hailstones with curved index and thumb of right hand.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: To denote hair of human being, touch hair of head.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold flat left hand out in front of breast with back out; lay lower edge of right hand on upper edge of left, resting at knuckle of left index, back to right and front, fingers extending, touching; move right hand to right and outwards.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: half of body one kind, half of another). Place flat right hand upwards, in center of breast, little finger near breast; move hand one foot to left, then back and one foot to right. Have seen Sioux make the sign “One- half Indian, one-half white man.”
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold flat right hand palm outward, in front of body, height of shoulders; move hand sharply to front and downwards, stopping it suddenly. Some Indians raise the hand higher for emphasis.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for BEAUTIFUL.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (to) (meaning: as pendant). The left index is extended and held horizontally in front of body, other fingers closed, and the right index curved and hooked to it.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for GLAD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold out left hand palm, straight up; strike it with right fist two or three times.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Bring right hand, back outwards, in front close to and a little above head, index and thumb spread and nearly horizontal, other fingers closed; lower the hand until thumb and index are about opposite the eyes; spread thumb and index, passing down close to forehead, index to left, thumb to right.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for AXE and SMALL.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for POSSESSION.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for BIRD; then hold partially compressed right hand a little higher and in front of right shoulder; move swiftly to front and down with slight curve up, imitating a hawk's dive through the air after its prey.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Point right index at person indicated.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for SICK, by imitating throbbing in front of head.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: First indicate gathering in from the sides, then bring hands upwards in curve to show the shape.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold right cupped hand behind right ear.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Bring compressed right hand pointing downwards over heart.
entries.author: Tomkins

headword: HEAVEN Point upwards with right index, looking up with reverence
entries.sign: (Modern.)
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: cannot hold up). Hold out flat hands in front of body, palms up; raise hands slightly and let them drop a few inches.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for WORK and WITH.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Point right index at person indicated.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for SIT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (to). Hold out left flat hand, pointing oblique to right; hold right hand in same relative position, pointing at left hand; then pass right down under left.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold right flat hand, back up, in front of right shoulder; then raise or lower to height desired to be shown.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for MOUNTAIN and LITTLE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Point to person and make sign for POSSESSION.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold both hands, back out, with fingers spread; lay the fingers of one hand over the interstices of the other, as if to prevent anything passing through be- tween the fingers; move the hands, held in this position, slightly to right and left, by elbow and shoulder action.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make circle with thumb and index of both hands; then, holding left in posi- tion, press compressed right through hole.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Pass palm of hand over face and make sign for BAD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for TRUE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold left flat hand edgewise, back to left in front of left breast. Some Indians to make the sign more emphatic place the right index and second fingers astride the left hand. The sign used in illustration is most generally used.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for HORSE and for RACE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for HOUSE, SICK, and MANY. Some Indians make signs for HOUSE and MEDICINE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: rays of sun pressing down). Hold flat hands above head, few inches apart; then bring hands down and slightly towards head.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: corner of log house). With hands in front of body, interlace fingers near tips, fingers at right angles, horizontal. This is the primitive sign for house, though Cheyennes frequently indicate shape of gable roof with both 5 hands pointing up.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Sign INTERROGATE or QUESTION: point left hand at 45 deg angle to right and front; then with index of right hand strike little finger and others in succession. As fingers are struck they remain down.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Expressed by HOW MANY. How much money would be, how many dollars?
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: See COUNTING.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: cuts one in two). Hold little finger edge of hand against center of body; then move to right and left as though cutting in two.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for WOLF, that is bring 2 hand near eye and move it around.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for WORK, and FAST.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for MALE, and MARRY.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: myself). With right extended thumb touch center of breast.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for WATER, for COLD, and bring hands together as in FREEZE OVER.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for WATER, for COLD, and hold right index in front of body, pointing downward.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for CANNOT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: seizing hold of). Hold left fist, back to left, a little higher and in front of left shoulder; then seize left wrist with right hand and pull it some inches to right; then cross wrists in front of body, right on top, hands closed.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: For a person “in my house,” make signs for HOUSE and SIT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold hands out in front of body, palms toward each other, few inches apart, fingers pointing to front; separate hands and move them out and apart by gentle jerks.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold the flat left hand, back up, in front, and rub it from wrist to knuckles, back and forth, twice.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for WHITE, SOLDIERS and WALK.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: doing evil to). Referring to someone else, make signs for WORK and BAD. Referring to one's self, make the signs for DO, TO ME, BAD.

entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Form an incomplete circle with thumbs and indexes of both hands out in front of body, ends of thumbs and indexes an inch apart; leave left hand in posi- tion, and make sign for WATER with right hand; then with tips of compressed right hand draw a circle outside the circle first formed.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: elbowing to one side). Hold closed hands near right and left breasts; move right elbow a little to right and rear, then left elbow a little to left and rear. Repeat.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold right hand with back down, in front of mouth, fingers separated, partly curved and pointing forward; move hand to front and upwards. This is a recog- nized Indian sign, but not in general use.

entries.sign: Make signs for HEART and GLAD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold compressed right hand, with back to right, close to right shoulder, fingers pointing to front; move hand to front, upwards, over, and down in vertical curve.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: For persons or officers this is generally indicated as in INFERIOR. The tip of one index lower than the other, the distance determining the difference in rank.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With right hand grasp left index firmly and move hands slightly to right and left.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for GOOD and CLOSE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for HALT, and repeat; then by lowering the hand gently the meaning would be, “Fear not,” “Do not be anxious,” etc.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Form an incomplete circle as in ISLAND; then with left hand in position carry partially-closed right hand across and down over imaginary kettle, making motion as though about to lift it by the handle.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Bring right hand in front of right shoulder, hand nearly closed; strike to front downwards and a little to left, stopping hand suddenly with slight rebound.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: near or distant from one source). Bring tips of extended, touching first and second fingers of right hand against lips, as in sign for BROTHER; then make the sign for CLOSE or DISTANT, as relationship may be.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: cutting a piece of meat, held with the left hand and with teeth). Hold right flat hand close to face, lower edge just over mouth; move the hand upwards and to left two or three times, as if trying to cut with lower edge of hand. Sometimes left hand is held in front of and a little higher than right, as though holding meat.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold right hand, back up, close to left breast; sweep hand outwards and slightly upwards, turning hand by wrist action until palm nearly up; thumb and index extended, other fingers closed, thumb and index horizontal, index pointing nearly to left, thumb pointing to front.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for KNOW, then open hand and sweep it to the right, making the sign NO.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: water and shape). Make sign for WATER; then with thumbs and index fingers make an incomplete horizontal circle with space of one inch between tips; then swing wrists together, tips of indexes apart.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: limping motion of animals). Hold closed right hand, palm down, one foot in front of right breast; move hand slightly to front, and by wrist action bend the hand downwards and to left, repeating motion.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Push both flat hands toward the ground, then spread them sideways.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for BIG, and if very big, add sign for HIGH.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for ROPE; then make as though to swing and throw same for- ward; then draw the hand back quickly as though catching the animal.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Bring right and left indexes together well out to left of body, representing a race; then pull right hand away back, representing last in the race.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for WINTER and BEYOND.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold both 5 hands partly closed, in front of both breasts, palms up; then move them up and down.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for TRUE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (to) (meaning: leading a pony with lariat). Hold closed right hand, back to right, in front, close to and a little higher than right shoulder; move the hand to front by gentle jerks.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for TREE; then hold right hand out in front of shoulder, index and thumb curved, one inch between tips, other fingers closed, back of hand nearly to right, lower edge pointing to front and upwards; give a wavy motion to hand to represent leaf on limb of tree.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Pass hands upwards over that portion of legs covered by leggings, thumb and index spread, backs of hands outwards.

entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (not heavy). Hold extended flat hands, back down, at same height in front of body, few inches apart, fingers pointing to front; raise hands briskly by wrist action.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (not dark). Make the sign for DAY.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: zigzag flash). Point right index upward; then move hand to right, rear and downwards in jerky motion, to imitate lightning flash.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for EQUAL.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold right 4 hand, cupped near right ear; turn hand slightly back and forth by wrist action.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold right hand at height of shoulder, back to right, end of thumb pressing against inner surface of index, so that only the end of index is seen beyond the thumb nail.

entries.sign: See TALK.

entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold right hand, fingers nearly extended and separated, over breast.

entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold hands well in front, to right and left of body, fingers curved and point- ing to front; move hands towards each other on vertical curve downwards; move them slightly upwards as though grasping hands, and finish full movement with hands opposite and few inches apart.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (also, EVERY LITTLE WHILE). Hold left forearm horizontally in front of left breast, pointing front and right; touch forearm of left several times with side of tip of extended index of right hand, other fingers and thumb closed, back of hand nearly to front; commencing near left wrist and moving hand towards elbow. This is also used to mean: OFTEN, ALL THE TIME, and WHILE.

entries.sign: (meaning: trade or purchase). Make sign for TRADE; then join index fingers, side by side, pointing to front.

entries.sign: Make an incomplete circle with thumb and index of right hand, spaced one inch between tips, other fingers closed, and place little finger on center of breast.

entries.sign: Make the sign for WINTER and for MIDDLE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: of birds). Make sign for BIRD, MANY and FLYING to south or north.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Touch the two first fingers of right hand to forehead.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold slightly compressed hands out in front of body, opposite neck, hands pointing upward, close together, move them one about the other in circles, sur- faces touching.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold up flat right hand with palm twelve inches from face, fingers point- ing upwards. This represents a hand mirror.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: half white man, half dog). Pass the spread thumb and index finger of each hand, other fingers closed, over and near the surface of body from waist upwards, palms towards body; then make sign for WHITES; then pass the hand similarly from waist down, and make sign for DOG. The upper portion like white man, lower like dog.

entries.sign: Make the signs for DAY and SUNRISE.

entries.sign: With partially curved compressed right hand give two or three gentle taps or pluckings at left breast.

entries.sign: This is a strictly recent proposition, and must be so regarded. The modern Indian, however, knows all about the pictures, and thousands act in them. Have seen different descriptive signs made, the most common being to ex- tend both flat hands, upright, and vibrate them rapidly, to show flicker of the picture, and sign LOOK. One Indian who had been to Hollywood made sign similar to OWL, as though looking into opera glass, and then sign for turning crank.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Partially curve the hands and, with backs up, bring them alongside each other in front of body; separate the hands in downward curves, to right with right hand, to left with left.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Push up the closed hand as in bluff, but raised higher; then make the sign for HARD. Use both hands to represent a mountainous country.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for CAT, for LONG TAIL, and for JUMP.

entries.sign: Make the sign for MANY.

entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for POSSESSION.

entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for TALK.

An ancient oath, with eyes and hands (flat) upraised, meant “God see my hands, they are clean.” Holding up the right hand is now understood by all Indians, and is called “The white man's way.”

Hold right hand near top of right ear, thumb, index and second fingers extended together; lower the hand while making a small spiral with tips of fingers. There is a general custom among all plains Indians.of decorating the hair with strips of otter skin.

entries.sign: Make the sign for POSSESSION.

entries.sign: With fingers extended rub the cheeks and front of face with palm of right hand.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Bring the hands close to breast, back up, then shake them with a quivering motion.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for WHITE MAN, for SOLDIER, and for WALK. Some- times add RIDING HORSE BACK, and GO.

entries.sign: If one-half, make sign for HALF; if more or less indicate accordingly.

entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Clasp the hands in front of body, with back of left hand down.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Compress fingers of right hand tightly together, cone shape; then raise hand in front of body, back outwards.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With right hand make as though to wind it up; then show turning disk; then make signs for LISTEN, and GOOD. (A flexible modern sign, well understood by Indians.)

entries.sign: Make the sign for GUN; then with both hands indicate “six”, for six shooter, by holding up right hand, fingers and thumb extended, separated, and holding up left thumb, left fingers closed.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Both 1 hands, backs up, carried outward and downward to- wards another person.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold both 1 hands, well out, and draw them to the breast.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for CORN, for WORK; then with right hand near shoulder make as though dropping seed in the ground.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold extended 5 hands well out to right and left; then bring them in to- gether as though gathering something up.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for HORSE and LITTLE, showing height with left flat hand.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (in possession). Hold up left 1 hand, back out, index pointed upwards; then with right index make as though to scrape left index bare, striking from tip of finger downwards.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Show size of animal; then point up with fingers as in grass; then indi- cate working on moccasin.

entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WHITES, for CHIEF, and for BIG, and with 1eft hand point afar as if towards Washington.

entries.sign: With closed right hand held in front and above right shoulder, shake the hand as if it was a rattle. (The rattle is an important musical instrument in Indian ceremonies.)
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for SNAKE; then extend right index upwards in front of right shoulder and vibrate sharply.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (to). See ARRIVE THERE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for BOOK and LOOK.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for POSSESSION.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Place right 1 hand before right breast, back up, forearm horizontal; raise the hand until forearm straight up, turning hand until back is to front. This means recovery from sickness or escape from danger.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: paint used on face). With fingers pointing upward, rub right cheek with inside first joints of right hand, making circular motion.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for SIT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for HEART, and KNOW.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for OFTEN.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for HOLD, and for KEEP QUIET.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for CHARGE, to show the attack; then by wrist action turn the hands so that fingers point to rear.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for POSSESS, MANY, PONIES (or HORSES).
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: If animal is meant, make the sign for HORSE, and then move hands forward in small curves. If riding a vehicle make the sign for same, and then make sign for SIT on left palm.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (finger). Hold left 5 hand in front of breast, lying flat, back up; then touch back of finger on third joint with right index.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for person; then hold left hand at height of neck, palm outwards, index pointing upwards; bring extended index of right hand beside and lower than left; raise right slowly until well above other hand.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: water flowing). Make the sign for water; then move right hand to left of face, height of neck, index extended pointing left, move hand to right until opposite right shoulder, with index horizontal.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With both open hand palms up. alternately push hands back and forth. A modern sign gives TRAIL and WAGON.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for HARD, and indicate shape.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold hands as in AFTER; then with tip of right index make a spiral curve by wrist action while drawing right hand to rear.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold slightly compressed left hand out in front; then with right compressed pluck at ends of fingers.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (to). Make the sign for WALK and for FAST.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold flat left hand in front of breast, back out; hold right in same relative position but nearer body; move right briskly so that back strikes inside of left hand.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for MEDICINE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: heart laid on the ground). Make the sign for HEART; then swing hand out and downwards toward the ground, turning palm up.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Place inside of both wrists together in front of breast; then holding this position, push both closed hands as far back as possible.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Touch the tongue with tip of extended right index, other fingers and thumb closed; then make the sign for BAD. Sometimes the sign for WHITE is made.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for EQUAL.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WHITES, for SOLDIER, and with right index mark position, extent and number of stripes on the arms.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Imitate using the tool.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for HOUSE, for WHITES, for LOOK (2 fingers pointing towards left palm), and for KNOW.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for TALK and BAD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WOLF.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (to). Make the sign for WOLF; then sign for LOOK.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: See SCOUT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: The usual names for the seasons are, WINTER, SPRING, SUMMER, FALL, and for explanation of same see pages 57, 49, 51, 23.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Bring right 2 hand to opposite eyes, and the two fingers should point in the direction one is looking.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Move open hands out in front of body; close them briskly and draw towards body, as though seizing something.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: See EXCHANGE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold the 1 hands close together in front, indexes pointing forward; by wrist action turn the hands so that right index points to right and front, left index to left and front; moving right hand to right and front, left to left and front.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold flat left hand, back to left, in front of body; use right index as an awl or needle, bringing it just over thumb, pointing to left, inner surface pressed against inner surface of index; move right hand slightly to left, and by wrist action turn back of index down as it passes. Repeat motion two or three times.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Clasp hands in front of body. In former times Indians only clasped hands in concluding a treaty or making peace. They now, in dealing with whites, observe the custom.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold flat right hand, back down, in front of right breast; then lightly touch lower edge of right hand with ball of left thumb; then make sign for GOÓD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for FEMALE; then sign for BLANKET.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WOMAN.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning; horns). Compress and slightly curve the hands in front and above the head-have them curve in a way similar to that made by the big horns of the sheep.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for MOUNTAIN SHEEP, for WHITES, and for WITH.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make thě signs for MOCCASIN and WHITES.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold nearly closed right hand, back up, in front of breast, tips of first three fingers pressed against ball of thumb; move hand out, down and to left. while snapping the fingers out from under the thumb.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold compressed right hand to right and front of body, fingers pointing upward and hand at height to be represented.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: sheep eater). Make the sign for INDIAN. for SHEEP, and for EAT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold extended 5 hands in front of body; then wave them out and in, two or three times, to denote throbbing.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold out flat left hand, back up, touch back of fingers with inside of fingers of right hand; then reverse this process; then make sign for TALK.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Place tips of fingers of right hand over lips, and incline the head slightlv to front.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for MONEY and WHITE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: See AFTER.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold right 2 hand in front of mouth and make sign for ALL.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: cutting off heads). Draw right flat hand across, from left, in front of neck as though cutting off the head. This is the sign of the Sioux or Dakota Nation.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for FEMALE; then place the tips of extended index and second finger against lips, fingers horizontal, backs up, other fingers and thumb closed; move the hand horizontally several inches to the front.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for BROTHER, for HIS, and for WIFE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold closed right hand in front of and little below right shoulder; then move hand downward several inches.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold the 1 hands, backs down, in front of body, equally advanced, several inches apart, indexes curved, move hands forward simultaneously.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Lower the extended flat hands with a sweep into following position: left hand in front of right breast pointing to right, right hand six inches to right of left, pointing to front and right; then incline head to right.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With both palms facing and three inches apart, move hands slowly forward by short stops.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: If referring to an animal, indicate the height. For small quantity of any- thing make the sign for FEW.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Bring right 2 hand, fingers separated, back up, in front of chin pointing to face; then by wrist action move the hand upwards, so that nose passes between tips of fingers.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: For distant or signal fire smoke, make sign for FIRE, and continue raising hand until higher than head.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: to smoke a pipe). Hold left fist in front of body; then with flat right hand held three inches above left strike down two or three times; then make sign for PIPE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for PRAIRIE, and add ROCK or BLUFF, and WIPED OUT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold right 1 hand at right side, waist high, move hand one foot forward with a wavy motion.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold extended 5 hands in front of face, fingers pointing downward, lower in circular zigzags, to indicate whirling, sifting snow.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Indicate the shape and size with right index; then make signs for WALK, SNOW, and GOOD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With hands held in front of body, rub them together as though washing them.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for HARD and NO.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Bring closed fists in front of breast, thumbs touching; then separate hands horizontally to right and left.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for man; then with right index pointing upwards, lower hand to in- dicate height of child.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Touch something yellow and make sign for LITTLE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With tip of extended index of right hand touch the tongue; then make sign for BAD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: See TALK.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for BUFFALO, and leaving right hand in position touch it with left; then use right hand to dip into some vessel, and carry to mouth.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold out flat left hand and arm, pointing right and front; then hold right hand above left wrist, fingers slightly separated; then with right finger tips start- ing at left wrist, touch left forearm every two inches towards elbow, merely brushing with ends of fingers. Southern Indians lay back of hands on each other, fingers over fingers, then rub them back and forth several times, to represent spotted, mottled, brindle, roan, or any off color.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: grass coming out of ground). Make the signs for GRASS and LITTLE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: a spring of water). Make the sign for WATER; then with thumbs and index fingers form a circle in front of body; then, still holding left in position, bring compressed right under the circle, fingers held under the thumb; then release them with a snap to indicate bubbling spring. Repeat last movement.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WOLF.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: To indicate anything standing upright, bring right 1 hand to right and front and higher than right shoulder, index pointing upwards.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: an agency on the MISSOURI RIVER). Make the signs for STAND and ROCK.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for NIGHT; then form a small incomplete circle with right thumb and index, and raise hand toward sky. For brilliant star, snap index against thumb to denote twinkling.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for GO.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for SIT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold extended left hand in front of left breast, back up, pass right 1 hand under and close to left hand, until right wrist is close to left palm, right index ex- tended; then draw back the right hand, at same time crooking index.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: fire-boat). Make the sign for BOAT; then sign for FIRE, holding hand a little higher than the head.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for HEART and FEW.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for HARD, and indicate shape as of a boulder.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: See HALT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for HOUSE and TRADE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: See TRUE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold left flat hand out in front of left breast, back down; use right hand like a hatchet and strike palm of left. Generally used to represent a blow given with a weapon.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold left arm as in SPOTTED; then draw palm of extended right hand from left to right across left forearm in various places.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: The sign for BRAVE was formerly used by many. The later preference is to hold right fist above left fist and strike over and downwards with twisting motion, as though breaking a small stick.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Touch the tongue with tip of right index; then make the sign for GOOD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for GRASS, holding hands very high. Some Indians also denote SUN passing overhead, and HOT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Form, with index and thumb of right hand, an incomplete circle, space of one inch between tips; hold hand towards the east; then move it in a curve across the heavens towards the west. Also used to denote the time of day. (Right hand held towards left indicates eastward).
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for DAY and MEDICINE. Have seen Indians describe other days of the week by indicating so many days before or after Medicine Day.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With right index and thumb make an incomplete circle, other fingers closed. Hold arm horizontal pointing to left; then raise hand about a foot.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With thumb and index of right hand forming an incomplete circle, extend right hand to right, about 1 foot above horizontal; then lower same 12 inches.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: In comparing two persons or things, place the two extended indexes side by side, pointing up, one held higher than the other, the highest representing the superior. When one is superior to several, place index of right hand above extended thumb and four fingers of left.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: See EAT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for ASTONISH.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold thumbs and indexes in semi-circle several inches apart and op- posite each other; then bring them together to form a flat circle.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: See SUGAR.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WATER; then strike the arms out well in front as though swimming.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Place right 1 hand to rear of center of body, index finger pointing to rear and downwards.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Push the right 1 hand well out in front, to right of body, index extended, pointing to front; pull hand quickly towards body while curving index finger into a hook.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: A “little talk”, or “one person talking to another”, is expressed as follows: with nail of right index pressing against thumb, move hand a trifle to front and snap the index straight forward (these words “are thrown out”). Repeat motion. For a council to “speak at length”, hold right flat hand, back down, in front of mouth, and move hand outward a few inches; repeating the motion.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold right hand as in STAND, but at full length of extended arm.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Move the hands, one about the other, with fingers slightly separated.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Touch the tongue with tip of right index.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Compress the right hand, and tap with ends of fingers that portion of body which has been marked.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for TREE, for LEAF, for DRINK, and for GOOD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With index fingers, touching at tips, form an angle of 60 degress. Some- times index fingers are crossed at first joints, to indicate extended teepee poles.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for WRITE; then hold flat hand back out, in front of breast; with lower edge of extended right hand strike upper edge of left, with a re- bound, and then make sign for GO, quickly. A flexible modern sign.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning bring the word to me). The open right hand is placed palm up in front of mouth; then draw toward the lips with a quick jerk.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Extend both flat hands, backs up, in sweeping curve outward and downward, toward another person.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for SIT, moving the hand well out from body. Have seen Indians simply point with middle finger.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Point to person and make sign ALL.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold up flat left hand sideways in front of breast, with right hand reach around from below and clasp thickest part; move thumb and finger back and forth few times.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for PERSON and for STEAL.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: If possible point to something thin; otherwise with right thumb and two fingers rub lower edge of left hand just back of little finger. This is a somewhat confusing sign, as it also stands for BACON. If making sign for BACON, add the sign EAT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: drawn from the heart). Hold right hand, back up, against left breast, index extended and pointing to left; move hand horizontally outwards eight or ten inches, turning palm downward.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for HUNDRED and for TEN.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: As though twisting thread rub innner surface of tips of thumb and index; make the sign for SEW, ending by carrying right hand well out to right to imitate motion of sewing.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for BIRD, and for FIRE, holding the hand a little in front of and higher than head. (Indian lore records thunder as being caused by the “Thunder Bird”.)
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: There has been some diversity of gesture in regard to passage of time, but we present the most logical. For abstract TIME, extend right and left 1 hands towards the left, hands tandem, then pull right hand about three inches backward to right. See BEFORE, AFTER, FUTURE, PAST, BEHIND and LONG TIME.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for COWARD, and LITTLE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold out 1 hands together, backs up; lower hands a few inches while drawing them slightly towards body.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold the flat left hand, back down, in front of body; place lower edge, or heel, of closed right hand on left palm; then with heel of right hand rub left palm with a circular motion.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for DAY and NOW, Many Indians merely use NOW.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WITH.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Generally indicated by using right forearm and hand as a hatchet, by elbow action, striking forward and downward with flat hand held edgewise.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for NIGHT, then sign for DAY; then with left hand indicate SUN rising in east.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Protrude tongue a trifle and touch with first finger.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: the wind charges). Make the sign for WIND, and for CHARGE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for CITY and LITTLE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WALK and point to the ground.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for EXCHANGE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for WHITES, CHIEF and TRADE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (to). Make the signs for TRACK and LOOK.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: For iron or steel traos, touch or point to something made of metal; hold closed hands side by side, knuckles touching, index fingers curved and touching; then bring sides of indexes together, to represent closing of jaws of trap.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: If the treaty is between two tribes make the signs for MAKE, SMOKE and SHAKE HANDS. If treaty is with the whites, make signs for SHAKE HANDS and WRITE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold open left hand about ten inches in front of shoulder, back outward, thumb and fingers spread. Move slightly upward, slowly, to indicate growth.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for the animal; then bring both fists in front of body, same height, equally advanced, and few inches apart; then imitate action of front feet in trotting by alternately striking to front and downwards.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for HEART; then hold right 5 hand over heart, palm almost touching, and by wrist action vibrate as in PERHAPS.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning; one way or tongue straight). Hold right 1 hand, back up, under chin, close to neck; move index finger straight to the front. This means straight from heart and tongue.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for PUSH.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: beard). Make the sign for BIRD; then place compressed right hand under chin, pointing downwards; vibrate hand slightly by wrist action.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With tip of thumb and index, make as though same were a small pair of tweezers; then indicate pulling out hair from face or eyebrows with a jerk. This is a constant practice with Indians.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for STAR, and while holding hand in that position snap index and thumb as in LITTLE TALK.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Pass the palm of flat right hand in a circle close to face; then make the sign for BAD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for PERHAPS.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for PERHAPS.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for KNOW.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WITH.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for MEDICINE and BAD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Point upward with right index.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for ME, ALL.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for INDIAN and for BLACK, and rub the face as in RED.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for WHITES, MEDICINE, MAN, and with extended right index finger strike left arm between shoulder and elbow.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for LOOK, pointing in different directions and moving hand rapidly; then signs MUCH, SLEEP, NO.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for TEEPEE, and for MANY.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: wheels). Hold hands, backs down, at equal distance in front of body, four inches apart, index fingers curved, others and thumb closed; indicate motion of wheels by making small circle with indexes.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (COVERED). Make the sign for WAGON; then hold both flat hands, backs up, indexes touching, height of face, and sweep them out and down in a curve to indicate wagon top.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for ROAD and WAGON.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make sign for HALT, but more gently and not stopping abruptly. Repeat gesture.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: motion of feet). For a person, hold flat hands in front of body equally advanced; move right to front, upwards and downwards describing an oval circle; move left to front in same way; as left is brought down draw right hand to rear and repeat first motion, thereby alternating the motions of the feet. For an animal, close the hands and make same motions as above.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning. give me). Hold the right hand close to chin back to right, form an unclosed circle with thumb and index, back of index at height of mouth, half inch space between tips of index and thumb, plane of circle vertical; move hand in slight curve downwards, outwards and upwards; turning hand by wrist action, ending with little finger as high as index.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for FIGHT.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Carry the flat hands from front to rear, close to sides of head, fingers pointing upwards, palms toward head; then carry right hand from top of head well down to rear of body.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Show the size of war-club stone; denote rawhide covering of handle by clasping left index with right hand; then strike to front and down with right hand.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for WAR, and DANCE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for MAN, and WAR.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WATER; then by motions imitate the act of washing.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: See DESTROY.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With thumb and index of left hand form a horizontal circle; then hold right index over same and move tip around the indicated circle; make sign for LOOK pointing at circle; make sign for KNOW, and for SUN-all of which indicates size of watch, movement of hands—by looking at same you will know where the Sun is.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: drinking out of palm of hand). Hold the cupped right hand, back down, in front of and little above mouth; fingers pointing to left and upwards; then move hand downwards, turning palm towards mouth. At end of RIVER or LAKE some Indians make the sign of dipping a handful of water with right cupped hand, held waist high.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for I or ME and ALL.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make signs for STRONG and NO.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for QUESTION, for HOW MANY, and indicate whether SLEEPS, MOONS, or WINTERS.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: what point). Make the sign for QUESTION, then point with right index in different directions.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: With closed right hand strike from front to right and rear, as though riding a horse and whipping him with a quirt.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for FIRE and WATER.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for COLOR; then rub with tip of right index the small segment at upper end of left thumb nail, or point to something white.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: cap wearers). Hold right hand to left of face on level of eyes, back up, index pointing to left; draw hand over to right side, index finger passing across above the eyes.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for WHITES and for MAN.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for INTERROGATE or QUESTION, but turn the hand very slowly.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold hands several inches apart in front of body, indexes extended and lapping; from this position change the hands, back up, edges pointing to front. fingers separated and slightly curved, move hands downward on curve.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for FEMALE and MARRY.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for BY ITSELF.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: I will). Make the sign for PUSH.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold the hands with backs up, near body at height of shoulders, and with wavy motion move the hands in direction of the wind.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold up the closed hands in front of body, forearms vertical, hands several inches apart; then give a shivering, tremulous motion to hands. With most Indians a year is called a winter, or one cold.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: See EXTERMINATE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: (meaning: heart and head both good). Make the sign for HEART, touch fore- head, and make sign for GOOD.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold flat left hand, back to left, in front; bring side of extended right index against center of left palm, index pointing to front.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Hold the right hand with palm outwards near right shoulder, first and second fingers extended and separated and pointing up; move the hand several inches to front and upwards.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for FEMALE and indicate height.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for MEDICINE.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the signs for TREE and CHOP.
entries.author: Tomkins

entries.sign: Make the sign for BIRD; then hold 1eft forearm about vertical in front of left shoulder; now bring partially compressed right hand and place it near elbow of left forearm, right side; move hand with a jump to left side; then to little higher up, showing manner of hopping around a tree; then lower left hand and tap palm several times with tip of curved index of right hand.

entries.sign: Bring flat hands in front of body edgewise, few inches apart, right hand higher and back of left; then raise and lower the hands by wrist action, to indicate working.

entries.sign: Hold right 1 hand in front of body; move hand briskly towards body, turn- ing index finger to left or right so that it grazes surface of body.

entries.sign: Bring slightly compressed hands, backs outward, in front of body, backs of fingers of right hand resting against palm of left, fingers horizontal; then move hands around each other in rotary motion.

entries.sign: Hold flat left hand, back to front and down, out in front of body, fingers pointing to right; then as if with pencil between thumb and index of right hand, make as though writing on left palm.

entries.sign: Make the sign for WINTER, for this year add sign for NOW.

entries.sign: (meaning: bowing the head and body). Hold right hand, back to right, in front of right breast, height of shoulder, index extended and pointing upwards, other fingers nearly closed, thumb resting on side of second finger; move the hand slightly to left and a little downwards, at same time closing index over thumb.

entries.sign: Make sign for NIGHT; then, still holding left hand in position, sweep the right upwards and to right in a semi-circle, until it is at same height as left hand, terminating with back of hand down.

entries.note: This work would be incomplete without some reference and information regarding the Indian “moons” or months. We have approached this subject with hesitation, because the Indian moons cor- respond only in a general way to our own months and with certain tribes the names vary greatly. The following moons, or months, are those adopted by the American Indian Association after careful study, and are approved as being most nearly correct by Dr. Charles Eastman, Strong Wolf, Running Bear and other prominent Indians. Where two or more names are given for the same month, we have selected the one which can be gestured and pictured most easily, and is most generally used.
